title: The Rise and Rise of Alice Huang - The Wire China
gist: Investigation tracing alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang (Huang Le) from offshore video-game deals tied to Shanghai Hexi and Century Huatong to running Megaspeed, a Singapore Nvidia partner that bought billions in AI servers and is under U.S./Singapore chip-smuggling probes; the affair with Jensen Huang triggered a board inquiry, ~10% NVDA drop, congressional pressure, and (per editor's note) his ouster on November 12 despite an earlier spokesperson statement that he would stay. Byline in raw is Ella Apostoaie; text bio names Noah Berman.

insights.claim: In 2019 Alice Huang made $145 million selling her BVI holding company Osmanthus Vale Holdings to Hong Kong-listed Shenzhen game developer 7Road Holdings, a company whose revenue had been just $36,000 in 2016.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Outsized valuation for a near-revenue-less shell is a red flag for related-party or nominee dealing around 7Road.
insights.quote: made $145 million from the sale of an online gaming group that three years earlier had annual revenues of just $36,000

insights.claim: Osmanthus's revenue jump from $36,000 in 2016 to $36 million in 2018 is likely explained by a Hexi-backed fund buying Hangzhou Shengfeng from Century Huatong in 2017 for 500 million yuan (about $75 million) and moving it offshore under Osmanthus in 2019.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Shows the deal was a restructuring of existing assets via offshore vehicles, not organic growth.
insights.quote: That acquisition could explain the exponential jump in Osmanthus’ revenues

insights.claim: Osmanthus was incorporated in the British Virgin Islands less than two months before 7Road bought it, and Shanghai Hexi was listed as its 'ultimate holding company'; how Huang came to own 100% of it is unclear.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Points to Huang as a possible nominee holder for Hexi interests.
insights.locator: Osmanthus, Ms Huang’s video-game investment vehicle

insights.claim: Huatong acquired a 10% stake in 7Road in December 2020, the same month it founded data-center subsidiary Shanghai Longjing, where Huang served as a director in 2021-2022.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Links the gaming groups, data-center assets and Huang in an interlocking network.

insights.claim: After October 2022 U.S. export controls barred 7Road from buying advanced Nvidia AI chips, it spun off its Singapore subsidiary 7Road International PTE, which could still buy them, selling it to a BVI company associated with Huang and renaming it Megaspeed.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Template for how Chinese firms route around chip controls via Singapore entities; expect enforcement focus on such structures.
insights.quote: 7Road decided to spin off its Singapore subsidiary, which could buy America’s best AI chips.

insights.claim: Megaspeed bought billions of dollars of servers with advanced Nvidia AI chips and is under U.S. and Singapore government investigation for possibly smuggling chips to China, yet Nvidia still listed it as an official partner as of November 11.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Partner-vetting failures could expose Nvidia to BIS penalties and restrictions on Southeast Asian sales.
insights.quote: As of November 11, Nvidia continues to list Megaspeed as an official partner on its website.

insights.claim: Megaspeed's assets jumped to $3 billion by end-2024 from $33 million a year earlier, after its shares were moved in November 2023 to Swiftdata Pte, a company incorporated weeks earlier whose sole director is Singaporean Tan Yong Pong.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: ~90x asset growth in a year signals the scale of AI-server purchases flowing through a single opaque Singapore vehicle.
insights.quote: By the end of 2024, Megaspeed’s assets had jumped to $3 billion, from just $33 million the year prior.

insights.claim: Megaspeed says there is no evidence of illicit chip transfers or illegal activity, while the Commerce Department's BIS declined to say whether it is considering measures against the company.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Watch for a BIS Entity List action against Megaspeed and related entities.

insights.claim: Desmond Shum argues Huang appears to be a 'white glove', a nominee investor whose name appears on documents on behalf of others, given a career centered on restructurings, leveraged acquisitions and offshore holding companies before suddenly fronting a multibillion-dollar AI infrastructure business.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: If Huang was a front, the true beneficial owners of Megaspeed's chip stockpile remain unknown, widening the probe's scope.
insights.quote: suddenly emerged as the public face of [Megaspeed,] a multibillion-dollar AI infrastructure business

insights.claim: Huang began as a state-television news reporter before moving into finance and becoming executive director of Shanghai Hexi Investment Fund, whose founder Kang Wei was fined $375,000 by the CSRC in 2025 for improper disclosures using complex investment vehicles.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Hexi's disclosure history reinforces the opacity concerns around Huang's deals.

insights.claim: In 2023 Shanghai's government announced Shanghai Longjing would build a 6,000-AI-server-rack data center at a complex where Tencent rents rack space filled with its own chips, a complex Songjiang district says will offer 10 times the computing power of the world's largest supercomputer.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Ties Huang's network to major Chinese AI compute capacity; Tencent denies any stake or operational role.
insights.quote: Shanghai Longjing would build a data center with 6,000 AI server racks

themes.theme: Fallout for Nvidia and Jensen Huang

insights.claim: Nvidia's board announced an inquiry into whether Jensen Huang was the target of a 'foreign intelligence effort', after initially calling the relationship 'not unusual', and the share price fell about 10% over five days.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Governance shock and leadership uncertainty are direct drivers of NVDA drawdown.
insights.quote: Its share price has dropped around 10 percent over the past five days.

insights.claim: Per an editor's note, Jensen Huang was forced to leave Nvidia on November 12, a day after publication, contradicting the spokesperson's earlier statement that he was committed to staying on as CEO.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: CEO departure at the world's leading AI chipmaker is a major leadership-transition event for NVDA and the AI supply chain.
insights.quote: Mr Huang was forced to leave Nvidia on November 12, a day after this article was first published.

insights.claim: The scandal has prompted a bipartisan senators' push for congressional investigations into Nvidia and tighter controls on AI chip sales to China, plus a request from three Republican committee chairmen for a closed-door briefing on November 18, and an FBI inquiry Trump mentioned.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Raises odds of reversal of loosened controls (e.g., on the H200), hitting Nvidia's China revenue.

insights.claim: Nvidia has long lobbied to weaken export controls on China sales, and Trump loosened controls on Nvidia's H200 chip last year, policy gains now at risk from the scandal.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: H200 China sales are the most exposed revenue line if controls retighten.
insights.quote: President Trump loosened controls on Nvidia’s H200 chip last year.

insights.claim: Former CIA Beijing station chief Randal Phillips says seducing visiting foreign executives is a common Ministry of State Security tactic and that most MSS resources were devoted to compromising private-sector interests.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Counterintelligence risk for executives of China-exposed firms is a real governance issue boards may now price in.
insights.quote: when you flew over the Pacific, that didn’t make you any better looking.

insights.claim: The scandal overshadows Trump's Asia trip to summits in the Philippines and China, with Trump saying Jensen Huang told him he knew of no intelligence links for Ms Huang; China's foreign ministry denied she worked for the MSS.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Could complicate U.S.-China summit outcomes on tech and trade.
insights.quote: The scandal will hang over the president’s Asia trip next week
